newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares rise on mounting optimism.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares rise on mounting optimism.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed higher on Thursday, fuelled by expectations the EU association treaty would be ratified which traders hope may bring foreign capital back to the market.

"If the Constitutional Court says the ratification is in line with the constitution, the index may rise by about five percent in a week. If not, prices could fall by up to 50 percent short-term," said Andrej Obed, a trader at A bank.
The SBI index rose 0.59 percent or 7.79 points to 1,323.34 taking its gains to nearly two percent this week.

An analyst said the ratification of the agreement would show Slovenia's intent on joining the EU and thus harmonise its legislation with EU standards. This should help stabilise the market and attract international investors, he said.
Overall five shares rose, seven fell and three were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover crumbled to 66 million tolars from 179.7 million tolars.
"I expect average daily turnover to at least triple if foreign investors return to buying," Obed said.
Food maker Kolinska was the most active share, easing 0.10 percent to 1,903 tolars on volume of 9,803 shares for total turnover of 18.7 million tolars.
Bank SKB was the top gainer, rising 3.47 percent to 49,150 tolars on volume of 18 shares on a technical rebound following last week's almost seven percent fall.
Dolenjska Bank led the day's decliners, tumbling 5.23 percent to 14,120 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
The bank on Tuesday decided to postpone the decision on whether to enable a 15-percent foreign ownership in the bank until the new banking law is passed.
Analysts said the law was expected to be adopted by parliament later this year.
